chapter_theme: One song at Kosainagar (கோசைநகர்): the poet asks not to wander in desire for women's bodies but to think each day of the feet whose anklets resound with the hundred crore Vedas.

699.reading: The poet asks that he not wander with great desire for the women's bodies where all of Kama's arts and play are born, but that grace come so that he thinks every day of the great lotus feet whose anklets cry out with a hundred crore Vedas. The praise names Siva, who wears the cool moon, the serpent, arugu grass, the feather and Ganga in his matted hair, the sharp vel given for Siva's glory, the death of the demons, Valli and Devayanai on either side, and Murugan beloved of devotees at Kosainagar.
699.nuance: நாத சதகோடி மறை ஓலமிடு நூபுரம்: the anklets of the feet sound the Vedas, so the feet are where scripture itself cries out. The opening names the woman's body plainly (திரிகோணம்) as the place where Kama's arts arise.

links.note: 699 asks to think daily of the feet whose anklets cry out a hundred crore Vedas (நாத சதகோடி மறை ஓலமிடு நூபுரம்). Tirumanthiram 898 makes the paired feet the eight letters and the paired anklets (கழலிணை) fifty-one and seven thousand, the letters and the mantras. Both hear scripture in the Lord's anklets: 699 as their sound, Tirumular as a count of letters.
